sources.entry: Hivemind by activeloopai - Hivemind turns your traces into reusable skills across agents

summary.one_liner: Hivemind is a cloud-backed shared memory layer that captures coding-agent sessions as traces and mines them into reusable SKILL.md skills shared across a team's agents.
summary.what_it_does: It captures each session's prompts, tool calls, and responses as structured traces stored in Deeplake, and provides hybrid lexical plus semantic search over those traces and skills, falling back to ILIKE lexical search when embeddings are off. A background worker mines traces for repeated patterns and writes them as SKILL.md files scoped to a workspace, and generates AI-written wiki summaries of sessions at session end. It exposes a virtual filesystem under ~/.deeplake/memory/ backed by SQL, and supports per-directory .hivemind files to route or disable capture. Integrations are provided for Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Cursor, Hermes Agent, pi, and Claude Cowork (Alpha). The README also describes shared team rules, goals, a codebase graph, generated code docs, and bring-your-own-cloud storage on GCS, Azure, or S3.
use_cases: share agent memory across a team's coding assistants
reuse solutions a teammate's agent already worked out
search past agent sessions for bugs or decisions
auto-generate skills from recurring coding patterns
keep agent sessions in your own GCS, Azure, or S3 bucket
route a client repo's agent traces to a separate workspace
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | sh  (macOS/Linux; URL truncated in README)
hivemind install --only claude  (or codex, claw, cursor, hermes, pi, claude_cowork)
git clone the repo, npm install, npm run build, npm test  (development)
notable: Skillify: mines team sessions into SKILL.md files that propagate to every connected agent
Works across Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Cursor, Hermes, pi, and Claude Cowork via per-agent hooks, plugins, or MCP
Per-directory .hivemind / .hivemind.local files route traces to an org/workspace or disable capture
Wiki summaries generated by shelling out to the host agent's own CLI, so no separate API key is needed
BYOC option to keep data in the user's own cloud storage
caveats: Optional semantic search adds about 600 MB of dependencies and is off by default; without it search is lexical only
Claude Cowork support is Alpha and only captures Local Agent Mode sessions, not plain desktop chat
Codex requires manually trusting hooks on first launch or hooks will not run
All users in the Deeplake workspace can read captured data by design
BYOC is listed as available for GCS and Azure, with S3 'contact us' and on-prem on request
